title: Adaptive Reporting Deadlines with Provisional Endpoint Classifications and an Unknown Reporting Clock
banked_reason: Math referee PASS, but field contract is not delivered: the global boundary-preserving experiment and sharp feedback-control values remain open; novelty gate assigns incremental with paper_score_ceiling 5.2<7.4. Independent terminal validity confirms below-floor.
gap_reasons: The promised focal object—a globally indexed, boundary-preserving original-record limit experiment with honest decision transfer and its limiting values—is explicitly left open; the delivered finite rate/length orders are a weaker kernel and cannot support the stated theorem-level positioning.

The claimed all-adaptive deadline-design frontier is not delivered beyond rate exponents: the sharp critical and regular control values, deterministic-mixture comparison, and attaining adaptive certificate are left unresolved.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier subfield is capped at incremental.
proof_attempt_summary: Attempted the joint weak-classification/short-reporting experiment and all-adaptive deadline frontier. Informal proofs of matched finite-budget risk and honest-length orders, nuisance benchmarks and the concentration elbow passed the math referee, but the original global moving-boundary experiment/decision transfer and sharp feedback-control certificates remain explicitly open. No Lean formalization was reached; both independent terminal consultations confirm incremental achievement below the field floor, so the run is downgraded with re-raise reserved for new proofs of those missing objects.
tldr: A provisional classification of a mature endpoint and a longer reporting window provide distinct information when both the classifier and outcome-dependent reporting clock are unknown. The focal object is the global joint marked-clock experiment, including completion counts, pending classifications and moving boundary constraints. The finite-budget targets certify the best precision attainable by every adaptive deadline controller and quantify when same-record classifier calibration removes the precision advantage of concentration. Honest connected intervals cover the entire stated model; a regular Gaussian Wald law is not presumed.
gap: Static shadow identification and irregular static inference, regular informative-reporting inference, and regular adaptive representations do not determine the globally curved experiment when classifier separation and reporting windows vanish together. A generic predictions-versus-label-cost motivation is already occupied.
fill: The project joins the global experiment and honest decision transfer to a matched all-controller frontier, with public equal-window and supplied-nuisance comparisons. The concentration advantage is a quantitative function of \((N,H,b,\kappa)\), not an assertion that longer windows are always preferable.
